chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Columbia people: Goddard Lieberson, John Hammond; Kenton at Capitol
summary: He praises Columbia's Goddard Lieberson and John Hammond's support, comparing it to Capitol's backing of Stan Kenton.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: So this is why I feel that -- and then, of course, the man who was so great at Columbia Records, whom I didn't mention earlier because I was only concerned with really the pop department, the man, Goddard Lieberson, who was head of the serious department and so on, and a very artistic man and a man who really treated the whole music thing with dignity. I'm glad I had the good fortune to be associated with some of these people. John Hammond was there, who really wasn't into our band because we were a little too far out for him. But he
would still be enthusiastic about for everything we did. And if you've ever had the feeling of having a company behind (unintelligible), you, we did. That was very important in those days.
Just as -- I would say in comparison would be with Stan Kenton and the way Capital believed in him and worked and allowed him his head, with him (unintelligible).
